text.overview: Federated Suns infantry benefit from one of the strongest industrial bases in the Inner Sphere, with AFFS quartermasters able to supply platoons with standardized equipment and ammunition from a logistics network that few rival states can match. Motorized platoons ride light vehicles that give them the speed to screen advancing columns, patrol supply routes, and respond to threats faster than foot infantry, though they sacrifice protection for that mobility. Armed with standard ballistic assault rifles, the most common and affordable infantry weapon in the Inner Sphere, these platoons deliver reliable short-range firepower and can be equipped and resupplied from almost any garrison stockpile.

Supplementing their primary arms with shoulder-launched short-range missile systems, these platoons carry enough anti-armor punch to threaten light vehicles and damage exposed BattleMech components at close range.

Conventional infantry within the FWLM serve as the backbone of provincial defense across a patchwork of semi-autonomous states, each maintaining its own military traditions and equipment preferences. Motorized platoons provide the speed the FWLM needs to cover the vast distances between garrison posts on provincial worlds, mounting troops on light vehicles that can respond to threats faster than foot infantry but without the expense of full mechanization. Armed with man-portable flamers that project streams of burning gel, these platoons carry one of the most psychologically devastating weapons available to conventional infantry. The short range and danger of carrying volatile fuel make flamer duty one of the most hazardous assignments in the platoon.

New technology and creative tactical thinking have long featured in FWLM infantry deployment, with varied unit types and specialized formations treated as the norm rather than the exception. Equipped with laser rifles that offer superior range and armor penetration compared to ballistic weapons, these platoons field one of the most effective personal arms available to conventional infantry, though the weapons are significantly more expensive and require soldiers to carry additional power packs.

text.overview: The Free Worlds League Military has long fielded some of the largest infantry formations in the Inner Sphere, with regiments numbering nearly 1,800 soldiers compared to roughly 750 in the Combine and just over 1,000 in the Federated Suns. Motorized platoons provide the speed the FWLM needs to cover the vast distances between garrison posts on provincial worlds, mounting troops on light vehicles that can respond to threats faster than foot infantry but without the expense of full mechanization. Carrying infantry-portable machine guns that deliver sustained automatic fire at close range, these platoons trade precision for volume, putting enough rounds downrange to suppress enemy positions and deny open ground to advancing troops.

The Free Worlds League's fractious politics have always made centralized BattleMech procurement difficult, pushing the FWLM toward heavy investment in conventional infantry to fill the gaps. Motorized platoons provide the speed the FWLM needs to cover the vast distances between garrison posts on provincial worlds, mounting troops on light vehicles that can respond to threats faster than foot infantry but without the expense of full mechanization. Armed with standard ballistic assault rifles, the most common and affordable infantry weapon in the Inner Sphere, these platoons deliver reliable short-range firepower and can be equipped and resupplied from almost any garrison stockpile.

The Free Worlds League's fractious politics have always made centralized BattleMech procurement difficult, pushing the FWLM toward heavy investment in conventional infantry to fill the gaps. Motorized platoons provide the speed the FWLM needs to cover the vast distances between garrison posts on provincial worlds, mounting troops on light vehicles that can respond to threats faster than foot infantry but without the expense of full mechanization. Equipped with infantry-portable short-range missile launchers, these platoons pack anti-armor punch that standard rifle or laser formations cannot match, capable of threatening light vehicles and even damaging BattleMech leg actuators at close range.

The Armed Forces of the Federated Suns equip select infantry formations with Thunderstroke gauss rifles produced by Federated Arms, giving these platoons range and armor penetration that conventional ballistic weapons cannot match. The Federated Suns' industrial base supports fielding such expensive personal arms where other states could not, and the AFFS expects a return on that investment through superior lethality at extended range. Supporting each squad is a Grand Mauler gauss cannon, a crew-served magnetic accelerator weapon that provides genuine anti-vehicle capability. The combination of gauss weaponry across both primary and support roles makes these formations among the most lethal conventional infantry in the Inner Sphere. Maintaining gauss ammunition stocks and the delicate magnetic accelerator components requires the kind of well-organized logistical support that AFFS regimental combat teams are specifically designed to provide.

The Federated Suns fields some of the most respected infantry in the Inner Sphere, with the AFFS treating its foot soldiers as essential partners in the combined-arms doctrine that defines the Regimental Combat Team. Among the most specialized of these formations, the Cerulean Mountain Infantry trains extensively for high-altitude and rough-terrain operations. Known as the "Goat Men," these troops can establish command posts on sheer cliff faces and launch attacks from approaches that conventional forces consider impassable. Their equipment includes re-breathers that allow them to operate at altitudes where conventional aircraft and VTOLs struggle to maintain lift. Armed with assault rifles and light missile launchers, the mountain troops combine vertical mobility with enough firepower to threaten light vehicles and exposed BattleMech components from unexpected angles.

309.name: Mountaineer 45th Cerulean Mountain Infantry; 3rd Davion Guards

text.overview: The Battle Corps Legion maintains one of the most unconventional intelligence assets in the mercenary world: the Baker Street Irregulars. Named after the fictional street urchins employed by Sherlock Holmes, the Irregulars are composed of young battlefield refugees from across the Jihad who can pass for teenagers or even younger children. Armed only with auto-pistols and carrying surveillance and communications equipment, the Irregulars are not intended for direct combat. Instead, they specialize in urban infiltration, exploiting the simple fact that few people pay attention to children. Operating in civilian clothes through city streets and occupied zones, these scouts gather vital intelligence that the Battle Corps cannot obtain through conventional reconnaissance. The Irregulars performed several critical intelligence operations during Operation SCOUR, and the Battle Corps has often credited their survival to the information these unconventional scouts provided.

310.name: Scout Infantry The Battle Corps - Baker Street Irregulars

text.overview:
The Skåret assassins of the JàrnFòlk are among the least verifiable infantry forces reported in the Periphery. What little is known comes from ComStar Explorer Corps reports and crime scene evidence gathered in the Hanseatic League. The JàrnFòlk themselves are Deep Periphery traders and explorers of Rasalhague descent who settled four systems within the Vela Nebula during the twenty-fifth century. Their society maintains no standing army and fields no BattleMechs or combat vehicles, making the existence of trained kill teams all the more unusual.

Rumors that surfaced in the late 3060s describe Skåret operatives working in teams of three or more, employing sniper rifles for long-range kills and blades, pistols, and poison for close work. Their ability to evade detection suggests access to sneak suit technology rivaling that of DEST operatives. Some intelligence reports indicate that at least some Skåret are exiles from JàrnFòlk society who sell their skills to the highest bidder, though whether the assassins truly exist remains an open question.

Warrior House Dai Da Chi, the most bellicose of the Capellan Warrior House orders, has trained an elite squad of snipers armed with the Minolta 9000 Advanced Sniper System. Originally custom-built for the Death Commandos, the Minolta 9000 is a precision instrument capable of eliminating targets at extreme range with minimal signature. These seven-trooper squads operate on foot with camo sneak suits, relying on fieldcraft and patience rather than speed or firepower. Dai Da Chi snipers have fought on several Republic worlds, building a grim reputation for identifying and eliminating enemy commanders. RAF forces along the Capellan front have been forced to devote significant counter-sniper resources in response to confirmed kills attributed to these squads.

312.name: Sniper House Dai Da Chi Snipers

text.overview: Com Guard fleet marines are trained for shipboard security, boarding actions, and combat in both zero-gravity and pressurized hull environments. When ComStar revealed its hidden WarShip fleet in the 3050s, the Inner Sphere learned that the Order had maintained a corps of fleet marines for decades, crewing vessels that most powers believed extinct. These marines are armed with Sunbeam laser pistols for close-quarters shipboard work and Blazer rifles for engagements where greater firepower is needed. Several ship-to-ship battles during the Jihad devolved into boarding actions, and Com Guard marines proved adept at repelling enemy assault teams and conducting offensive hull breaches. The Republic Armed Forces' own WarShip-based marine units drew significantly from Com Guard marine doctrine, which remains the benchmark for Inner Sphere naval infantry training.

313.name: Space Marine Com Guards Warship Fleet Marine

text.overview:
Stone's Trackers trace their origins to the 212th Nova Cat Headhunter Binary, a clandestine Clan Nova Cat unit formed during the Jihad for missions too dishonorable for conventional Clan warriors. The 212th joined Devlin Stone's coalition in 3071 and spent the remainder of the war conducting high-risk assassination, sabotage, and counterinsurgency operations against the Word of Blake. Inner Sphere personnel filled the ranks alongside the original Clanners as casualties mounted, creating a hybrid unit that embraced unconventional tactics regardless of cultural origin.

After the Jihad, the 212th was officially transferred to the Republic Armed Forces and rechristened the 212th Special Operations Battalion. The transfer stripped the unit of its BattleMech and battle armor elements over the objections of its founding commander, making the Trackers a purely infantry formation. Stone's Peace left few opportunities to maintain combat readiness, and many veteran operators retired. The Capellan Crusades provided the first real test of the rebuilt unit, and the Trackers saw heavy action during border skirmishes with the Confederation. The fighting crippled the battalion, and the 212th was officially disbanded following the Crusades. Surviving operators were reportedly distributed across RAF SpecOps Command to spread their headhunting expertise throughout the Republic's special operations community.

The Citizens' Militia is the backbone of Taurian planetary defense, drawing on a tradition of citizen-soldiery older than the Concordat itself. Organized under the Concordat Constabulary, the paramilitary force responsible for reinforcing Taurian defenses in wartime, the Militia represents the armed populace that every Concordat world can call upon when threatened. Though last in priority behind the regular TDF, noble family regiments, and the Constabulary, the Militia's sheer numbers and stubborn determination have turned the tide on more than one occasion.

These foot platoons carry the Zeus heavy rifle, a hard-hitting ballistic weapon that compensates for the Militia's lack of advanced training with raw stopping power. Support squads operate light SRM launchers that give even these part-time soldiers a credible anti-armor punch at close range. The combination of heavy personal arms and missile support makes the Citizens' Militia a genuine threat to any attacker foolish enough to dismiss Taurian civilians as noncombatants. National service requirements ensure that most Taurian adults are qualified riflemen, and the fierce patriotism that has defined the Concordat since the Reunification War burns as hot in the Militia as in any TDF line regiment.

315.name: SRM Foot Infantry Taurian Citizens' Militia

text.overview: The Eyrie Defense Force guards the most sensitive intelligence facility in Free Worlds League space: the Eagle Corps headquarters, a hidden bunker beneath a dead volcano on Wendigo, the airless moon of Atreus. The Eagle Corps served as SAFE's special-forces branch, and its protectors are drawn from highly skilled, xenoplanetary-trained soldiers who spend most of their time sealed inside space suits. Operating in standard platoons of twenty-eight, the EDF carries gyroslug rifles paired with ER support lasers, giving each platoon a 360-meter engagement envelope and enough concentrated firepower to give pause to even BattleMech pilots. This firepower comes at a cost. The weight of their armament prohibits anti-BattleMech operations entirely, and the troops must devote significant effort to redeployment between positions rather than engaging on the move. After the dissolution of the Free Worlds League, the Marik-Stewart Commonwealth retained the Eyrie and its defenders, though SAFE itself splintered into competing factions across the successor states.

316.name: Xenoplanetary Infantry Eagle Corps Eyrie Defense Force
